sessionName: Week 22 - Commercial model and margins revisited
summary: Luke Badiali revisited the commercial model with Chris and Leanne after a quarter of live data. Fixed fees worked on margin but two clients pushed back on paying upfront, and scope creep hit one engagement. We changed the pricing strategy to a base fee plus success fee, and replaced the 42% margin floor with a 45% floor.

discussion.keyPoints: Four new engagements were signed on fixed fees averaging 47% gross margin. One ran 20% over scope despite the change-control clause.
Two operating partners asked for part of the fee to be tied to EBITDA results. Chris now sees this as a selling point rather than a risk.
Actual business development cost came in at about £12k per new client, under the cap discussed in week 10.

recommendations.recommendation: Price 100-day plans as a £35k base fee per workstream plus a success fee of 10% of EBITDA uplift delivered, capped at £60k. This replaces the earlier fixed fee from £45k per workstream.
Raise the minimum gross margin to 45% before signing. This replaces the earlier 42% floor.
Cap business development cost at £15k per new client, tracked quarterly.
Model a base case of £5.2m fees next year and a downside where one core PE house drops out.

actions.action: Redraft the engagement letter for base plus success fee
Define how EBITDA uplift is measured with the operating partner

nextFocus: Test the base plus success fee model on the next two proposals.
nextPreparation: Leanne to bring the two live proposals priced on the new model.
